record_type_quote:
Experiment 1 in this thesis was a conceptual replication and extension of Sonbul
and Schmitt (2013).

targets.title:
Explicit and implicit lexical knowledge acquisition of
      collocations under different input conditions.
targets.evidence_quote:
As a conceptual replication, Experiment 1 aimed to confirm the generalisability of
Sonbul and Schmitt’s finding that repeated occurrences of low-frequency medical
collocations produced declarative knowledge of these collocations and that typographic
enhancement of the collocations produced more declarative knowledge than no
typographic enhancement. The present study also aimed to extend the findings of
Sonbul and Schmitt by increasing the number of encounters with the collocations in
context and extending the learning treatment from one to two days.
targets.outcome_quote:
Typographic enhancement led to greater
declarative (cued-recall) knowledge of prep+N collocations than no typographic
enhancement. This result was expected since bolded collocations in Experiment 1 and
Sonbul and Schmitt (2013) were learned better than unbolded collocations. What seems
likely is that bolding of prep+N combinations made them more perceptually salient to
the learners, drawing increased attention to the combinations and helping the learners
detect formal and semantic links between the prepositions and the nouns (Boers et al.,
2016; Choi, 2017; Sonbul & Schmitt, 2013).
        Unexpectedly, no difference was found between the amount of declarative
knowledge resulting from repeated exposure to V+N collocations in the typographic
enhancement and the no-typographic enhancement conditions.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Experiment 1 explicitly confirms the original non-native-speaker experiment’s declarative learning and typographic-enhancement findings (section 3.10.1.1). Experiment 2 extends the same empirical comparison to non-technical lexical and grammatical collocations: enhancement helps prep+N but not V+N collocations, explicitly departing from the expected original enhancement advantage (section 4.8.2). These comparisons support a mixed aggregate verdict across the thesis. The Experiment 1 declarative-only confirmation does not state a verdict on both thesis experiments as a whole. Procedural learning found after increased exposure is explicitly presented as an extension; it is not, by itself, the basis for mixed.

targets.title:
Second language lexical acquisition: A study of the development of
       collocational knowledge.
targets.evidence_quote:
My findings also partially corroborate Gitsaki’s
finding of lower scores in a gap-fill task for V+N collocations encountered previously
than for prep+N collocations encountered previously. In Experiment 2 of this thesis, a
larger amount of declarative knowledge of prep+N collocations than of V+N collocations
was gained when the combinations were made more perceptually salient through
typographic enhancement. However, no difference in gains for the two phrase types was
recorded in the no-bolding condition, meaning that in that condition they were equally
difficult to learn.
targets.outcome_quote:
My findings also partially corroborate Gitsaki’s

targets.outcome_reasoning: Experiment 2 empirically re-tests the specific earlier gap-fill finding that previously encountered V+N collocations yield lower scores than prep+N collocations. Section 5.3.6 explicitly describes partial corroboration: the original ordering holds with typographic enhancement but disappears without it. This is a specific comparison to an earlier empirical finding, beyond general agreement with claims about learnability. No DOI or original study number is supplied.

reasoning: Full source read sequentially, including both experiments, general discussion, complete references and appendices A–Q. The thesis reports new samples and completed results. Sonbul and Schmitt (2013), original Experiment 2 with non-native speakers, is the explicit replication target; both thesis experiments test its learning/enhancement claims, with Experiment 2 extending the materials and population. Gitsaki (1999) is also an empirical target because Experiment 2 directly checks its specified V+N-versus-prep+N gap-fill finding and states which condition corroborates it. Theory and interpretation suppliers (including Craik and Lockhart, Barcroft, Tomlin and Villa, Reichle and Perfetti, and the broad learnability claims of Howarth and Ackermann and Chen) are not separately coded. References providing tests, materials, item-selection procedures or statistical methods are not targets. General contextual comparisons with repetition, eye-tracking, ERP and glossing literature do not establish additional specific empirical retests; in particular, Hulstijn et al. (1996) supplies the glossing/elaboration rationale, rather than a separately replicated original design or finding. Experiments within this thesis are not counted as published original targets.
